A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the single-channel conductance of the ACh receptor channel is governed largely by the charge distributions flanking the M-2 transmembrane segment, and that the open time of the channel is influenced by multiple elements located at the amino termini and/or the M-2 segments of different AChR polypeptides.

the channel properties of the ACHR are governed by a number of different elements, some of which are located on the alpha-subunit, and others of which are located in the M2 domain of the beta- and delta-subunits.

the channel open time of AChR is determined by the M2 region and by the flanking regions of the channel-forming subunits, whereas channel voltage sensitivity is determined by the voltage-sensing subunits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the channel conductance and the channel open time are controlled by distinct regions of each AChR polypeptide.
the single-channel properties are not a simple function of the amino acid sequence of the transmembrane domain, but are also influenced by sequences flanking this domain.
the channel properties are influenced by the amino acid sequences flanking the M1-M2 loop, the M2 trans-membrane domain and the amino acid sequence in the C-terminal half of the subunits.
